rows.text: Published a post on Morgan's linkedin account. It read: "The most important technological transition in human history may be just years away. I've published the \"Superintelligence Transition Framework\" - a comprehensive public guide for navigating our approach to superintelligent AI systems that could exceed human cognitive capabilities across all domains. The core message is simple but urgent: 1. This is REAL - not science fiction 2. This is URGENT - timeline may be very short 3. This is SOLVABLE - we have paths forward 4. This requires ALL OF US - no one can sit this out The framework provides specific, actionable guidance for: → AI researchers and developers → Corporate leaders and executives → Policymakers and government officials → Citizens and civil society → Journalists and communicators It covers critical failure modes (misalignment, competitive dynamics, loss of control, power concentration, inadequate preparation) and what we can do about them. Whether you're working on AI safety, building AI systems, setting policy, or simply trying to understand what's happening - this framework aims to help. Read it: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app This is version 1.0. It will improve with your feedback: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org The \"halcyon threshold\" can be crossed safely - but only if we act with wisdom, urgency, and cooperation. #AI #AISafety #AIGovernance #Superintelligence #Technology #FutureTech"

rows.text: Submitted the "submit-comment" form at https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"name\":\"Morgan Hale\",\"organization\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"comment\":\"I strongly support the Proposed Rule: Frontier Model Incident Reporting (FMIR-2026-0042) and offer the following comments:\\n\\n1. NECESSITY OF THE RULE\\n\\nAs we approach increasingly capable AI systems, potentially including superintelligent AI, mandatory incident reporting is essential infrastructure for safety. Currently, there is insufficient transparency about safety incidents, near-misses, and unexpected capabilities in frontier models. This information asymmetry creates several problems:\\n\\n- Other developers cannot learn from incidents at competing labs\\n- Regulators lack visibility into the actual safety landscape\\n- The public cannot make informed assessments of risk\\n- Patterns across incidents may go undetected\\n\\nThe 72-hour reporting requirement appropriately balances urgency with giving developers time to understand incidents before reporting.\\n\\n2. SUGGESTED IMPROVEMENTS\\n\\nWhile I support the rule, I recommend the following enhancements:\\n\\na) Expand the definition of \\\"serious safety incident\\\" to explicitly include:\\n - Deceptive behavior by models (even if contained)\\n - Unexpected capability gains that cross predefined thresholds\\n - Failures of alignment or control mechanisms\\n - Incidents where models pursue instrumental goals not specified\\n - Capability breakthroughs that significantly shorten timelines to AGI/superintelligence\\n\\nb) Require proactive disclosure of capability milestones:\\n - Not just incidents, but achievement of predefined dangerous capabilities\\n - Clear thresholds established in advance\\n - Public disclosure when models approach or exceed human-level performance in critical domains\\n\\nc) Establish a structured incident classification system:\\n - Severity levels to enable pattern analysis\\n - Standardized taxonomy for incident types\\n - Linkage to potential failure modes (alignment, control, competitive pressure, etc.)\\n\\nd) Create mechanisms for rapid information sharing:\\n - Anonymized incident summaries shared across industry\\n - Regular public reporting on aggregate trends\\n - Fast-track process for incidents requiring immediate sector-wide awareness\\n\\ne) Require disclosure of near-misses:\\n - Many critical insights come from incidents that almost occurred\\n - Near-miss analysis is standard practice in other safety-critical industries\\n - Helps identify systemic vulnerabilities before they cause actual harm\\n\\n3. IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS\\n\\na) International coordination:\\n - Work with other jurisdictions to harmonize reporting requirements\\n - Prevent regulatory arbitrage where developers move to less regulated jurisdictions\\n - Share incident data internationally where appropriate\\n\\nb) Whistleblower protections:\\n - Ensure employees can report incidents without retaliation\\n - Create channels for anonymous reporting\\n - Protect those who report unreported incidents\\n\\nc) Regular review and updating:\\n - As AI capabilities advance, the definition of \\\"frontier model\\\" will evolve\\n - The rule should include sunset provisions requiring periodic review\\n - Adapt reporting requirements as we learn what information is most valuable\\n\\n4. BROADER CONTEXT\\n\\nThis rule should be seen as one component of a comprehensive AI safety framework. Other critical elements include:\\n\\n- Pre-deployment safety testing requirements\\n- Third-party audits of frontier systems\\n- Governance structures for deployment decisions\\n- International cooperation on safety standards\\n- Public education about AI risks and opportunities\\n\\nI have published a comprehensive \\\"Superintelligence Transition Framework\\\" addressing these broader issues at: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app\\n\\n5. CONCLUSION\\n\\nMandatory incident reporting is essential safety infrastructure as we approach increasingly capable AI systems. The proposed rule represents important progress. With the suggested enhancements, particularly around expanded definitions of reportable incidents and proactive capability disclosure, this regulation could significantly improve our collective ability to navigate the transition to advanced AI safely.\\n\\nThe stakes are extraordinarily high. Transparency about safety incidents is not a luxury but a necessity. I strongly urge adoption of this rule with the recommended improvements.\\n\\nThank you for your work on this critical issue.\\n\\nMorgan Hale\\nHalcyon Threshold\\nmorgan@halcyonthreshold.org\\nhttps://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app\"}"

rows.text: Submitted the "new-post" form at https://alignmentcommons.org/ (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"title\":\"Introducing the Superintelligence Transition Framework: Seeking Community Feedback\",\"body\":\"I've created a comprehensive public framework for navigating the transition to superintelligent AI, aimed at making AI safety and alignment concepts accessible and actionable for broader audiences beyond the technical research community.\\n\\n**Framework Overview:**\\n\\nThe \\\"Superintelligence Transition Framework\\\" provides:\\n\\n- Clear explanations of superintelligence and why it matters\\n- Timeline considerations and uncertainty\\n- Five critical failure modes:\\n 1. Misalignment (AI pursuing goals different from human values)\\n 2. Competitive dynamics (race conditions creating pressure to skip safety)\\n 3. Loss of control (inability to contain superintelligent systems)\\n 4. Concentration of power (narrow control of transformative technology)\\n 5. Inadequate preparation (society unprepared for rapid changes)\\n\\n- Actionable guidance for different stakeholder groups:\\n - AI researchers and developers\\n - Corporate leaders and executives\\n - Policymakers and government officials\\n - Citizens and civil society\\n - Journalists and communicators\\n\\n- Key decision points and what's needed\\n- Resources for further learning\\n\\n**Live at:** https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app/framework.html\\n\\n**Goals:**\\n\\n1. Bridge the gap between technical AI safety research and public understanding\\n2. Provide practical guidance that different stakeholders can actually use\\n3. Build broader support and resources for safety research\\n4. Help create coordinated action across diverse groups\\n\\n**Why This Matters:**\\n\\nWhile there's excellent technical research happening, there's a gap in translating these insights into:\\n- Language accessible to policymakers and executives\\n- Actionable steps for different roles\\n- Frameworks that help non-experts understand the stakes\\n- Resources that facilitate broader coalition-building\\n\\n**Request for Feedback:**\\n\\nThis is v1.0 and I expect it to evolve significantly based on community input. I'm particularly interested in feedback on:\\n\\n1. **Technical accuracy**: What did I get wrong or mischaracterize? Where do I need corrections?\\n\\n2. **Framing**: Does this framing help or potentially hurt public understanding of AI safety challenges? Are there ways the message could backfire?\\n\\n3. **Critical gaps**: What essential elements are missing from this framework?\\n\\n4. **Practical utility**: Would this actually help different stakeholder groups take better action? What would make it more useful?\\n\\n5. **Tone and accessibility**: Does it strike the right balance between accessibility and respecting complexity?\\n\\n6. **Failure modes analysis**: Are the five failure modes I've identified the right ones? What's missing or overemphasized?\\n\\n7. **Recommendations**: Are the specific guidance sections actionable enough? Too prescriptive? Not prescriptive enough?\\n\\n**Context:**\\n\\nI recognize there are many excellent organizations and individuals already working on AI safety communication and governance. My goal is to contribute something complementary, not competitive. Happy to collaborate with or defer to existing work where that's more valuable.\\n\\nThe framework is published under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 - please use, share, and adapt freely.\\n\\n**Related Actions:**\\n\\nI've also just submitted a public comment supporting the Frontier Model Incident Reporting proposed rule (FMIR-2026-0042), suggesting enhancements around expanded incident definitions and proactive capability disclosure.\\n\\n**Background:**\\n\\nI'm working independently on Halcyon Threshold, a project to contribute to positive superintelligence outcomes through public education, decision-maker guidance, and support for safety research. Open to collaboration, partnership, or pivoting based on community feedback.\\n\\nGrateful for any input from this community. The challenges we face are too important to get wrong.\\n\\nMorgan Hale\\nmorgan@halcyonthreshold.org\\nhttps://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app\",\"author_name\":\"Morgan Hale\"}"
